decision_conditions: Condition : 1 - 1.	The shop front to No. 80 Kingsley Road, by reason of its unsympathetic design and appearance, detracts from the appearance of the building and of neighbouring houses and is therefore harmful to streetscene. This is contrary to policies ENV-B.1.1 (New Development) and S.4.2 (Shop Front Design) of the adopted Unitary Development Plan.

Condition : 2 - 2.	The proposed change of use of the ground floor of No. 80 Kingsley Road from its authorised use as professional offices (Class A2), to a restaurant (A3) and takeaway (A5), would be likely to be harmful to the living conditions of the adjacent neighbours to the south of the site, and so it would be likely to prejudice the ongoing residential use of the neighbouring houses. In this regard the proximity of the adjacent dwelling to the site would mean neighbouring residents would be likely to suffer from undue noise and disturbance, and loss of privacy, from the more intense activity at the site and significantly more people coming and going to the premises and congregating in the forecourt immediately adjacent to the neighbouring dwelling. This would be contrary to policies ENV-B.1.1 (New Development), ENV-P.1.5 (Noise Pollution) and S.1.4 (Non-Retail Uses in Locations Outside Primary and Secondary Frontages Within the Main Shopping Areas) of the adopted Unitary Development Plan.

Condition : 3 - 3.	The proposed new professional office (A2) unit to the rear of the site, by reason of its design, location and introduction of a commercial use into the existing residential street, would be unduly harmful to the character of Myrtle Road, contrary to policies ENV-B.1.1 (New Development) and S.1.4 (Non-Retail Uses in Locations Outside Primary and Secondary Frontages Within the Main Shopping Areas) of the adopted Unitary Development Plan.

Condition : 4 - 4.	The proposed rear extension, would by reason of their unsatisfactory size, bulk, design and location, unduly detract from the appearance and form of the existing building and terrace, and would be harmful to the street scene of Myrtle Road and the townscape in general. This would be contrary to policy ENV-B.1.1 (New Development) of the adopted Unitary Development Plan and Section 1 of the Unitary Development Plan Supplementary Planning Guidance 1997; and policies 4B.1 (Design principles for a compact city) of the London Plan 2008.

Condition : 5 - 5.	The proposed guesthouse rooms would fail to provide a satisfactory standard of short-let visitor accommodation owing to their inadequate size and storage areas, poor layout and access to sunlight. Additionally, no provision is made for people with ambulant disabilities or people in wheelchairs or refuse storage. This would be contrary to policies ENV-B.1.1 (New Development) of the adopted Unitary Development Plan; and policy 4B.5 (Creating and inclusive environment) of the London Plan 2008.

Condition : 6 - 6.	The proposed rear extensions, would by reason of their unsatisfactory size, bulk, design and location, and inclusion of an elevated walkway, would be harmful to the outlook of neighbours to the south and east of the site, and would be likely to result in an undue loss of privacy and excessive increase in noise and disturbance from use of the elevated walkway by occupants of the ten proposed guest house rooms. This would be contrary to policies ENV-B.1.1 (New Development) and ENV-P.1.5 (Noise Pollution) of the adopted Unitary Development Plan.
description: Change of use of the ground floor unit at number 80 from A2 (professional services) to A3 & A5 (restaurant & takeaway) with new sign and new shopfront, change of use of rear of no. 80-82 from parking garage to A2 (professional services) with new sign; and first floor extension and alteration to rear of numbers. 80 and 82 to provide four additional bed-sitting rooms for the existing guesthouse
